teams.name: San Francisco 49ers
teams.desc: A 35-10 rout of Minnesota in Mexico City has writers calling San Francisco the league's best and most complete team, and quarterback Brock Purdy drew MVP talk after his three-touchdown night against a defense that had stifled everyone. The shared worry is the offensive line after right tackle Colton McKivitz fractured his ankle. Seattle visits Sunday for a key division game.

teams.name: Buffalo Bills
teams.desc: Buffalo has won six straight, and its defense has gone three games without allowing a touchdown, a franchise-record 43 straight drives. The caveat is that the run has come mostly against backup quarterbacks, and Josh Allen threw two interceptions in a 26-9 win over Miami. Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs visit on Thanksgiving night, the first real test for that defense.

teams.name: Kansas City Chiefs
teams.desc: Patrick Mahomes is back in the MVP conversation, with 13 touchdown passes and no interceptions over his past four games after throwing for 324 yards and three scores in a 34-7 rout of Arizona. Rookie running back Emmett Johnson has kept the run game going with Kenneth Walker III out with a groin injury. Next is a Thanksgiving night trip to Buffalo, which has won five straight regular-season meetings.

teams.name: Chicago Bears
teams.desc: Chicago has won five straight without trailing, and defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons, a deadline trade pickup, had three sacks in a 21-13 win over New Orleans. The worry is an offense that sputtered again, with Caleb Williams just OK and running back D'Andre Swift's fumbles drawing attention. The Thanksgiving trip to Detroit, with first place in the NFC North at stake, is the test everyone is circling.

teams.name: Denver Broncos
teams.desc: Rookie running back Jonah Coleman has given Denver the ground game it lacked, running for 111 yards and three touchdowns in a 38-24 win over Las Vegas, the sixth straight victory. The shared knock is that the wins are rarely pretty, Bo Nix remains inconsistent, and opponents keep outgaining the Broncos. Next is a Black Friday trip to Pittsburgh, and writers want to see better play on the road.

teams.name: Jacksonville Jaguars
teams.desc: A sloppy 23-18 loss to the Giants had writers questioning Jacksonville, as Trevor Lawrence threw two interceptions under constant pressure and the Jaguars committed 13 penalties. Others call it a one-game stumble, pointing to a Parker Washington touchdown that officials ruled incomplete and an AFC South lead that still looks safe. Tennessee visits Sunday, and left tackle Walker Little's fourth-quarter injury is worth watching.

teams.name: Detroit Lions
teams.desc: Detroit has won six straight, and Jared Goff and Jahmyr Gibbs carved up a strong Tampa Bay defense in a 31-21 win. Writers give the most credit to a defense that keeps improving without injured stars Aidan Hutchinson and Jack Campbell, with rookie edge rusher Derrick Moore adding pressure. Chicago visits on Thanksgiving with first place in the NFC North on the line.

teams.name: Cincinnati Bengals
teams.desc: A 22-20 Monday night loss at Washington snapped a five-game winning streak, and writers called it the worst the Joe Burrow offense has looked in a long time. Most still see a contender, noting the Bengals topped 30 points in five straight games before Monday. The Saints visit Sunday with the AFC North lead down to one game, and some rankings went out before the loss.

teams.name: Minnesota Vikings
teams.desc: The 35-10 loss to San Francisco in Mexico City shook faith in Minnesota's defense, which gave up three touchdowns on the first four possessions after carrying the team all season. Writers still rate the unit among the league's best, but the offense under Kirk Cousins did little, with red-zone struggles and two turnovers. Atlanta visits Sunday, the start of a stretch with five of the last seven games at home.

teams.name: Seattle Seahawks
teams.desc: Seattle comes off its bye with Sam Darnold back at practice, and coach Mike Macdonald has laughed off questions about sticking with Drew Lock, who played well in relief. The defense remains the calling card, with a streak of more than two years without allowing a 100-yard rusher. Sunday's trip to San Francisco looks season-defining, since the defending champions already trail by three games in the NFC West.

teams.name: Los Angeles Rams
teams.desc: Los Angeles won four straight before the bye, but receiver Puka Nacua's season-ending knee injury has writers asking where the offense comes from, with Davante Adams out until mid-December and tight end Terrance Ferguson also done for the year. The defense is the bright spot, allowing 12.3 points per game during the winning streak. The schedule turns brutal, starting with Green Bay on Wednesday night, then Kansas City and San Francisco.

teams.name: Green Bay Packers
teams.desc: Green Bay gets edge rusher Micah Parsons back for his season debut, nearly a year after his last game. The worry is an offensive line writers blame for the struggles and a run game that ranks last in the league, coming off a blowout home loss to Minnesota. Wednesday night's trip to the Rams feels like a playoff game, and running back Josh Jacobs is questionable.

teams.name: New York Giants
teams.desc: A 23-18 win over Jacksonville was New York's first over a winning team since Week 6 of last season, and writers now take John Harbaugh's team seriously behind a defense led by outside linebacker Abdul Carter's two sacks. The knock is an offense that barely moved, with J.J. McCarthy completing 47 percent of his passes and running back Cam Skattebo losing another fumble. Next is a trip to Indianapolis.

teams.name: Cleveland Browns
teams.desc: Cleveland gained ground during its bye and now holds the AFC's No. 6 seed, and writers credit a tough, well-coached team whose six wins have all come by four points or fewer under first-year coach Todd Monken. The shared knock is an offense that ranks 18th in passing and 24th in rushing. Next is a Sunday night home game against Las Vegas that the league flexed into prime time.

teams.name: Carolina Panthers
teams.desc: Carolina is back to .500 and two games clear in the NFC South after a 35-33 win over Baltimore, with Bryce Young and running back Chuba Hubbard delivering the final score. The defense gave up 421 yards and 33 points, a step back for a unit that had shown signs of life. A win at Tampa Bay on Monday night could all but lock up the division.

teams.name: Pittsburgh Steelers
teams.desc: Pittsburgh has lost two straight since its bye, and the 19-16 loss to Philadelphia brought receiver DK Metcalf's ejection and fresh calls to bench quarterback Aaron Rodgers. Writers still see a likely playoff team with a strong run game and a talented defense, but few think it can compete with the AFC's best. Denver visits on Black Friday, and the limited passing game needs answers.

teams.name: Houston Texans
teams.desc: The 26-3 rout of the Colts kept the Texans on the edge of the playoff race, and quarterback C.J. Stroud has writers talking about a second contract after his fifth straight game with multiple touchdown passes. Some discount a win over a collapsing Indianapolis team, and the 0-4 start leaves almost no room for another loss. The Ravens visit Sunday, with a trip to Pittsburgh next.

teams.name: Dallas Cowboys
teams.desc: The Cowboys scored on every possession but a final kneel-down in a 51-30 win over the Titans, and Dak Prescott threw for 325 yards and four touchdowns as the offense piled up 91 points in two weeks. The defense still draws the most worry, though writers saw more pressure in Mike Pettine's first game calling the defense. At 5-6, Dallas hosts the Eagles on Thanksgiving with the NFC East still in reach.

teams.name: Washington Commanders
teams.desc: Jayden Daniels outdueled Joe Burrow again as the Commanders upset the Bengals 22-20 on Monday night, with rookie receiver Antonio Williams making big catches and kicker Drew Stevens hitting the winning field goal for Washington. Writers also credit a suddenly stout defense and a team that kept fighting for embattled coach Dan Quinn. At 4-5-1, Washington sits two games behind the Giants, and a softer stretch starts Sunday at Arizona.

teams.name: Tampa Bay Buccaneers
teams.desc: A 31-21 loss in Detroit dropped the Buccaneers to 3-7, and writers keep pointing to a passing game that cannot move the ball while quarterback Baker Mayfield plays through thumb and foot problems. The defense remains the bright spot, and Tampa Bay is 2-0 in the division with an easy remaining schedule. Monday night's visit from the Panthers looks like a must-win in the NFC South race.

teams.name: Las Vegas Raiders
teams.desc: Rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza threw for 267 yards and three touchdowns in his second start, and writers see real growth even in a 38-24 loss at Denver. The rest of the picture is grim, with a long losing skid since the Kirk Cousins trade and a defense that has allowed 30 or more points seven times. The Raiders visit the Browns on Sunday night, possibly with tight end Brock Bowers back.

teams.name: New England Patriots
teams.desc: The Patriots come out of their bye at 5-5 without quarterback Drake Maye, who is likely done for the season with a fractured fibula, and most writers call it a lost year. A defense that has allowed more than 30 points in three recent losses and receiver A.J. Brown's hamstring injury add to the gloom. Tommy DeVito starts Sunday at the Chargers in what several writers call a must-win.

teams.name: Baltimore Ravens
teams.desc: A 35-33 loss at Carolina extended the Ravens' losing streak to six games, now the league's longest. Writers say quarterback Jacoby Brissett has the offense moving better without Lamar Jackson, but the defense under coach Jesse Minter has become the bigger problem, and 12 turnovers in four games have not helped. Sunday's trip to Houston before the bye looks like an elimination game.

teams.name: Atlanta Falcons
teams.desc: The Falcons come out of the bye at 3-7 after losing five of six, and writers keep circling back to shaky play from quarterback Michael Penix Jr. The odd bright spot is a weak NFC South, which leaves Atlanta just two games out of first despite the record. A trip to Minnesota, with a possible Kirk Cousins revenge game, opens a tough post-bye stretch.

teams.name: New Orleans Saints
teams.desc: Pressure is building on coach Kellen Moore after a 21-13 loss in Chicago dropped the Saints to 3-7, with 19 turnovers and an offense averaging fewer than 16 points over the past month. The defense earned credit for competing against the Bears, and the weak NFC South keeps New Orleans alive for now. The Bengals and Packers come next, and several writers see a reckoning ahead.

teams.name: New York Jets
teams.desc: The Jets snapped a five-game losing streak with a 27-24 win over the Chargers, scoring on every possession but kneel-downs. Rookie outside linebacker David Bailey, now at 9.5 sacks, and a young roster draw praise, though most writers expect coach Aaron Glenn to be gone and see three 2027 first-round picks as the real focus. A trip to Miami comes next.

teams.name: Philadelphia Eagles
teams.desc: The Eagles snapped a seven-game losing streak by beating the Steelers 19-16, as the defense sacked Aaron Rodgers five times and Saquon Barkley ran for a touchdown. Writers still see a lost 3-7 season, and some say the win only hurts Philadelphia's draft position. Quarterback Joe Milton III faces his former Dallas teammates on Thanksgiving, a game that could decide whether the NFC East talk is real.

teams.name: Indianapolis Colts
teams.desc: The Colts released quarterback Daniel Jones after a 26-3 loss in Houston, and writers call it the latest in a string of bad decisions, since the team passed on trading him only days earlier. Several add that running back Jonathan Taylor should have been dealt too. Anthony Richardson takes over at quarterback for a long look at his future, starting Sunday against the Giants.

teams.name: Arizona Cardinals
teams.desc: The Cardinals fell 34-7 at Kansas City with 40-year-old Josh Johnson as their fourth starting quarterback, and they have scored 16 points during a three-game losing streak. The team fired defensive coordinator Nick Rallis on Monday after allowing 30 or more points in four of five weeks. Some writers still like coach Mike LaFleur's attitude, and the schedule eases starting Sunday against Washington.

teams.name: Tennessee Titans
teams.desc: Coach Robert Saleh called the 51-30 loss in Dallas "disgusting football" and "embarrassing football," and the Titans have now allowed 40 or more points in three straight games. Quarterback Cam Ward is the bright spot, with multiple touchdown passes in three straight games, including one to rookie receiver Carnell Tate. At 1-9, Tennessee visits Jacksonville next with the 2027 draft looming large.

teams.name: Miami Dolphins
teams.desc: The Dolphins lost 26-9 in Buffalo for a fourth straight defeat, gaining just 185 total yards with backup quarterback Kyle McCord starting for the injured Malik Willis. Writers still praise how hard the team fights, from a defense that kept forcing field goals to a rookie class that plays beyond its years. At 1-9, Miami hosts the Jets on Sunday in one of its best remaining chances to win.

teams.name: Los Angeles Chargers
teams.desc: Any good feeling from the win in Baltimore vanished in a 27-24 home loss to the Jets, and writers now question whether coach Jim Harbaugh returns in 2027. Quarterback Justin Herbert threw two touchdown passes for his first multi-touchdown game in a long while, but he entered the concussion protocol afterward. The 1-9 Chargers host the Patriots on Sunday with Herbert's status uncertain.
